propositions: A vendored Dockerfile builds from the addono base by digest and starts a Jira 8.17.1 instance without pulling an unpublished image, using mandatory entrypoint flags -DskipAllPrompts=true and -Dproduct.start.timeout to survive cold starts and timeouts.

REST v2 readiness is verified via polling /rest/api/2/serverInfo on localhost:2990 with a 20-minute default timeout and 5-second cadence, overridable by environment variable, returning skip-not-fail when the harness is down.

Smoke tests create and read back issues via REST v2 and authenticate using programmatically minted Personal Access Tokens via Bearer authorization, proving DC auth semantics work against real Jira 8.x.

Teardown verifies deletion by polling direct issue endpoints (/rest/api/2/issue/{key}) to 404 without consulting the search index, per ADR 0037 discipline, and a session fixture detects and refuses to run against residual projects from prior incomplete teardowns.

The harness runs only on native linux/amd64 runners via a separate external-integration.yml job; local arm64 hosts experience severe emulation overhead and are unsupported, with acceptance evidence named by architecture.

The suite skips cleanly without REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 and a running instance, defines _live_jira_ready for canary participation, and the default suite excludes external tier entirely, verified by pytest collect-only.
